title: TSCP FCO Receipt Composition Algebra Model
description: The declarative model defining how receipts compose without creating authority, matching FCO_RECEIPT_COMPOSITION_ALGEBRA.md

receipt_type.description: Definition of the 7 receipt fields. NO authority field is present.

id.description: Content-addressed identity (SHA-256 hash of the receipt content)

subject.description: What the receipt is about (e.g., 'NTT backend equivalence')

items.description: Artifacts supporting the claim (test logs, hashes, proofs)

evidence.description: List of artifacts supporting the claim

claim.description: The assertion made by the receipt, supported by dependencies within a specific scope

dependencies.description: What evidence or prior claims support the statement

scope.description: The domain or context where the claim applies

lineage.description: Directed acyclic graph representing the provenance chain of how this receipt came to exist

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 representation of when the receipt was produced

signature.description: Cryptographic commitment to the receipt content

authority_exclusion.statement: No field named authority, permission, jurisdiction, execution_rights, or control exists in the receipt type.
proof: 1. The receipt type R is defined as the product of exactly seven fields: id, subject, evidence, claim, lineage, timestamp, signature.
2. None of these seven fields is authority, permission, jurisdiction, execution_rights, or control.
3. The only constructor for R produces a tuple of exactly those seven fields.
4. No field in the tuple has a type or subtype that can carry or represent authority.
5. Therefore, no receipt can structurally contain authority.

composition_preservation.proof: Since the composition operator (⊕) produces a receipt of type R, and type R excludes authority, the composed receipt r3 cannot contain authority. The composition operator preserves the structural type boundary.

subject_agreement.description: Receipts about different subjects cannot compose. This prevents unrelated evidence aggregation.

claim_consistency.description: Claims must not contradict. A receipt asserting P cannot compose with a receipt asserting not P.

lineage_acyclicity.description: Composition must not create cycles in the lineage graph, preventing circular self-justification.

evidence_independence.description: Evidence sources must be independent. Shared evidence must be explicitly declared in the lineage to avoid hidden self-attestation.

id.description: Content-addressed identity (SHA-256 of the composed receipt fields: subject, evidence, claim, lineage, timestamp)

subject.description: Preserved from component receipts (which are equal via subject_agreement guard)

evidence.description: Set union of the evidence lists from both component receipts

claim.description: Conjunction of component claims, governed by the claim_structure composition rule

lineage.computation: union(r1.lineage.nodes, r2.lineage.nodes, {r3.id}) and union(r1.lineage.edges, r2.lineage.edges, {(r3.id, r1.id), (r3.id, r2.id)})
lineage.description: A union DAG that adds the new composed receipt ID as a root with directed edges to both components

timestamp.description: The latest timestamp among the component receipts

signature.description: Cryptographic commitment to the composed receipt content

statement.description: What is asserted by the claim

dependencies.description: References to evidence supporting the assertion

scope.description: The applicability boundary or domain of the claim

composition_rule.description: The scope intersects (narrows), rather than unions (widens). The composed claim applies only where both component claims apply, preventing automatic strengthening.

drift_receipt.description: A negative receipt extension representing semantic drift or failure of a property under test.

statement.const: Property P failed under test T
statement.description: Statement representing a test failure assertion

dependencies.description: Identities of the oracle and test vectors used

scope.description: Boundaries or context where the failure applies

test_output.description: Log or stdout of the failed test run

oracle_output.description: Output from the reference semantic oracle

deviation_measurement.description: Quantified delta or error distance between implementation and reference

classification.description: Classification of the semantic drift to locate which layer moved (added to evidence items)

lineage.description: A combination of the oracle's custody chain and the implementation's custody chain

ImplementationDrift.description: The implementation diverged from the formal specification.

SpecificationDefect.description: The specification was unclear, leading to different valid interpretations.

OracleDefect.description: The semantic oracle or reference model itself contains an error.

LineageDivergence.description: Both the specification/reference and the implementation changed; neither is incorrect in isolation.

composition_rules: Negative receipts participate in composition under the same rules.
Subject agreement must hold (both receipts must address the same subject).
A negative receipt and a positive receipt about the exact same property under the exact same test are contradictory, making composition undefined.
A negative receipt about property P under test T1 and a positive receipt about property P under test T2 may compose, because they operate on different scopes (different tests).
